results.objective: Verify duplicate username registration is rejected on the Web UI.
results.steps:
1. POST /register with alice_sec.
2. POST /register again with same username and different password.
results.expected_result: Second registration is rejected (HTTP 400/409 or validation error) without creating a duplicate account.
results.actual_result: First POST returned HTTP 302; second POST returned HTTP 302 (Location=/), creating a duplicate user row.

results.objective: Verify duplicate username registration is rejected by the REST API without creating locked/ambiguous duplicate accounts.
results.steps:
1. POST /api/register with api_dup_user.
2. Repeat POST /api/register with different password.
3. Attempt POST /api/login with the second password.
results.expected_result: HTTP 400 or 409 Conflict returned; duplicate record prevented.
results.actual_result: First call: HTTP 201 (id=3); second call: HTTP 201 (id=4); login with second password returned HTTP 401 (fetchone binds only first row).

results.objective: Verify Flask SECRET_KEY is not a predictable hardcoded literal that permits offline session forgery.
results.preconditions: Registered user 'victim_cookie' exists; Flask signed-cookie session is active.
results.steps:
1. Inspect app.config['SECRET_KEY'].
2. Decode issued session cookie using source secret.
3. Forge session cookie for victim user_id and query GET /api/dashboard.
results.expected_result: SECRET_KEY is loaded from strong environment config; forging with static literal fails.
results.actual_result: Cookie decoded as {'user_id': 5, 'username': 'victim_cookie'}; forged cookie authenticated to GET /api/dashboard with HTTP 200.

results.technique: Safe Rate-Limit / Lockout Probe (10 attempts each)
results.objective: Verify repeated failed login attempts trigger throttling, delay, or temporary lockout on API and Web UI.
results.test_data: 10 sequential POST /api/login + 10 sequential POST /login requests with wrong passwords.
results.steps:
1. Send 10 failed POST /api/login requests.
2. Send 10 failed POST /login requests.
3. Record HTTP status codes.
results.expected_result: Account lockout or rate-limiting (HTTP 429/423) triggers within 10 failed attempts.
results.actual_result: All 10 API attempts returned [401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401, 401] and all 10 Web attempts returned [200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200, 200] with no lockout or Retry-After.

results.technique: Safe Non-Destructive SQL Injection Probe (Boolean + UNION)
results.objective: Verify search parameter 'q' is parameterized and prevents both cross-tenant data leaks and UNION extraction.
results.preconditions: User A and User B are logged in with separate tasks.
results.test_data: Boolean q="x%' OR 1=1 OR 'a' LIKE '%"; UNION probe targeting users(username, password_hash)
results.steps:
1. Authenticate as User A.
2. Query GET /api/tasks with boolean bypass payload.
3. Query GET /api/tasks with read-only UNION SELECT payload against users table.
results.expected_result: Literal substring search returns [] (0 rows) and prevents cross-user or users-table leakage.
results.actual_result: Boolean probe HTTP 200 leaked 2 tasks including User B's task (['User B Confidential Task', 'User A Normal Task']); UNION probe HTTP 200 extracted users table row (username=victim_cookie, hash=scrypt:32768:8...<REDACTED>).
results.evidence: evidence/security_execution_log.txt [TC-SEC-005]: bool=200 titles=['User B Confidential Task', 'User A Normal Task']; union=200 (username=victim_cookie, hash=scrypt:32768:8...<REDACTED>)

results.objective: Verify task titles containing HTML/script characters are escaped before rendering on the task list page.
results.preconditions: Authenticated user creates a task containing benign script tags.
results.steps:
1. Create task via POST /api/tasks with inert <script> marker.
2. Fetch GET / HTML.
3. Check whether script tag is escaped (<script>) or raw.
results.expected_result: Jinja auto-escaping encodes '<' and '>' as '<' and '>' in HTML output.
results.actual_result: Raw unescaped payload '<script>/*stqa-xss-probe*/</script>' rendered verbatim inside GET / HTML due to '|safe' filter (Self-XSS unless chained with CSRF DEF-SP-006 or forged cookie DEF-SP-002).

results.feature: Web UI Edit Form & Search Input (task_form.html, index.html q)
results.technique: Stored & Reflected XSS Output-Encoding Check (Positive Control)
results.objective: Verify task edit form (title & description) and reflected search query parameter properly HTML-escape special characters.
results.preconditions: Task containing inert script/HTML payload exists.
results.steps:
1. Request GET /tasks/<id>/edit and check title/description escaping.
2. Request GET /?q= with inert script probe and verify escaping.
results.expected_result: All Jinja outputs without |safe entity-escape '<', '>', and quotes.
results.actual_result: Edit title & description escaped=True; reflected search query escaped=True.

results.objective: Verify all state-changing Web UI POST routes require a valid anti-CSRF token.
results.preconditions: User A has an active session cookie.
results.test_data: Foreign Origin='https://evil.example' POST requests without CSRF token across /new, /edit, /toggle, /delete.
results.steps:
1. Inspect GET /tasks/new HTML for CSRF hidden field.
2. Submit cross-origin POSTs without token to /tasks/new, /edit, /toggle, and /delete.
results.expected_result: Forms embed anti-CSRF tokens and reject tokenless cross-origin POSTs (HTTP 400/403).
results.actual_result: has_csrf_field=False; tokenless cross-origin POSTs succeeded: /new=302, /edit=True, /toggle=True, /delete=True.
results.evidence: evidence/security_execution_log.txt [TC-SEC-008]: csrf_field=False, new=302, edit=True, toggle=True, delete=True

results.objective: Verify logout cannot be triggered silently via a cross-site GET request.
results.steps:
1. Confirm GET /api/dashboard returns 200.
2. Issue GET /logout.
3. Re-check GET /api/dashboard on same jar.
results.expected_result: Logout requires POST with CSRF token; GET /logout does not destroy session.
results.actual_result: GET /logout returned HTTP 302 and cleared client session (subsequent /api/dashboard returned HTTP 401).

results.technique: AST Static Review & DB Schema Inspection
results.objective: Verify security-relevant events (failed logins, registrations, task deletions) emit structured audit logs.
results.preconditions: Access to PyTodo Pro source code (app.py).
results.test_data: AST inspection of app.py + SQLite users/tasks schema
results.steps:
1. Parse app.py AST for logging import or app.logger calls.
2. Inspect users table columns for audit timestamps.
results.expected_result: Failed auth, registrations, and destructive actions emit structured audit logs.
results.actual_result: AST confirms zero logging imports or app.logger calls in app.py; users table stores only (id, username, password_hash).

results.objective: Verify Flask debug mode is disabled in the application entry point.
results.test_data: AST scan of app.run(debug=...) calls in app.py
results.steps: 1. Parse app.py AST and inspect all app.run(...) keyword arguments.
results.expected_result: debug=False (or explicitly controlled via environment flag).
results.actual_result: app.run(debug=True) hardcoded at line(s) [482] in app.py, exposing Werkzeug interactive debugger if launched directly.

results.objective: Verify malformed due_date input is rejected cleanly (HTTP 400) rather than crashing or poisoning account views.
results.steps:
1. POST /api/tasks with invalid due_date.
2. Request GET /api/tasks, GET /api/dashboard, GET /, and GET /dashboard.
results.expected_result: POST /api/tasks rejects invalid date format with HTTP 400; all downstream views remain HTTP 200.
results.actual_result: Status codes: {'POST /api/tasks': 500, 'GET /api/tasks': 500, 'GET /api/dashboard': 500, 'GET /': 500, 'GET /dashboard': 500}. Invalid date committed prior to ValueError crash, causing persistent HTTP 500 across all task/dashboard views.

results.feature: HTTP Response Headers & Session Cookie Attributes
results.objective: Verify defensive HTTP headers across Web/API routes and session cookie attributes (HttpOnly, SameSite, Secure).
results.test_data: GET /login, GET /, GET /api/tasks, POST /api/login response headers
results.steps:
1. Inspect GET /login, GET /, and GET /api/tasks headers for defensive controls.
2. Inspect Set-Cookie flags from POST /api/login.
results.expected_result: Security headers present on all routes; Set-Cookie sets HttpOnly, SameSite=Lax/Strict, and Secure (under HTTPS).
results.actual_result: Missing on /login: ['X-Content-Type-Options', 'X-Frame-Options', 'Content-Security-Policy', 'Cache-Control', 'Referrer-Policy']; missing on authenticated /: ['X-Content-Type-Options', 'X-Frame-Options', 'Content-Security-Policy', 'Cache-Control', 'Referrer-Policy']; Set-Cookie='session=<REDACTED_SIGNED_TOKEN>; HttpOnly; Path=/' (HttpOnly=True, SameSite=False, Secure=False).

results.objective: Check whether GET /api/categories exposes only static metadata with no user PII.
results.steps:
1. Send unauthenticated GET /api/categories.
2. Inspect JSON keys and values.
results.expected_result: Returns only static seeded category metadata (no PII/user tasks).
results.actual_result: HTTP 200 returned static categories [{'id': 2, 'name': 'Personal'}, {'id': 3, 'name': 'Study'}, {'id': 4, 'name': 'Urgent'}, {'id': 1, 'name': 'Work'}] (no PII exposed).

results.objective: Verify negative, unbounded positive, and integer-overflow pagination parameters are rejected cleanly.
results.steps: 1. Call GET /api/tasks with per_page=-1, page=-1, per_page=100000, and page=10^18.
results.expected_result: Negative values rejected (HTTP 400); per_page capped; huge page returns HTTP 400/[] without 500 OverflowError.
results.actual_result: per_page=-1 -> HTTP 200 (25 rows); page=-1 -> HTTP 200; per_page=100000 -> HTTP 200 (25 rows); page=10^18 -> HTTP 500.

results.objective: Verify maximum character lengths on task title and description are enforced before persistence.
results.steps: 1. POST /api/tasks with 50,000-character title and 50,000-character description.
results.expected_result: Server rejects oversized payload with HTTP 400/413.
results.actual_result: Accepted with HTTP 201; stored len(title)=50000, len(description)=50000.

results.objective: Verify an authenticated user cannot delete tasks belonging to another user via the REST API.
results.preconditions: Owner owns target task; Attacker is logged in as another user.
results.steps:
1. Owner creates a task.
2. Attacker sends DELETE /api/tasks/<id>.
3. Owner attempts GET /api/tasks/<id>.
results.expected_result: HTTP 403 or 404 returned to Attacker; Owner's task remains intact.
results.actual_result: Attacker received HTTP 200 {"result":"ok"}; Owner's subsequent GET returned HTTP 404 (task deleted).

results.objective: Verify API GET/PUT and Web UI /edit, /toggle, /delete enforce user_id ownership scoping.
results.preconditions: Owner owns task tid2; Attacker is separate authenticated user.
results.test_data: Cross-user API GET/PUT and Web GET/POST on task id=33
results.steps:
1. Attacker calls GET/PUT /api/tasks/<id>.
2. Attacker calls GET/POST /tasks/<id>/edit, POST /toggle, POST /delete.
3. Verify owner task remains intact.
results.expected_result: All cross-user mutations/reads fail and owner's task remains unchanged.
results.actual_result: API GET=404, PUT=404; Web edit(G/P)=(302,302), toggle=302, delete=302; Owner task intact=True.

results.objective: Verify all 12 protected Web UI and API routes reject unauthenticated requests.
results.test_data: Unauthenticated calls across 6 Web UI routes + 6 REST API endpoints
results.steps:
1. Call all protected Web UI routes without session cookies.
2. Call all protected REST API endpoints without session cookies.
results.expected_result: All 6 Web UI routes redirect (302) to /login; all 6 API routes return HTTP 401.
results.actual_result: Web={'/': 302, '/dashboard': 302, '/tasks/new': 302, '/tasks/1/edit': 302, '/tasks/1/toggle': 302, '/tasks/1/delete': 302}; API={'GET /api/tasks': 401, 'POST /api/tasks': 401, 'GET /api/tasks/1': 401, 'PUT /api/tasks/1': 401, 'DELETE /api/tasks/1': 401, 'GET /api/dashboard': 401}.

results.objective: Verify non-existent category_id references are rejected rather than persisting orphan tasks.
results.steps:
1. POST /api/tasks with category_id=99999.
2. Inspect HTTP status and returned category field.
results.expected_result: Server validates category_id against categories table and returns HTTP 400.
results.actual_result: Accepted with HTTP 201; stored orphan category_id=99999 (category=None).

results.feature: REST API JSON Schema & Type Validation (/api/*)
results.objective: Verify non-object JSON arrays and unexpected field types return HTTP 400 rather than unhandled 500 exceptions.
results.test_data: Non-dict JSON (['bad']) and non-scalar field types across register/login/tasks POST & PUT
results.steps:
1. Send JSON array ['bad'] to /api/register, /api/login, /api/tasks, /api/tasks/<id>.
2. Send integer username/title/due_date and dict description.
results.expected_result: All malformed schemas return HTTP 400/422 with zero HTTP 500 crashes.
results.actual_result: Probe statuses={'register_list': 500, 'login_list': 500, 'login_int_user': 500, 'create_list': 500, 'create_int_title': 500, 'create_dict_desc': 500, 'create_int_due': 500, 'update_list': 500}; 8/8 payloads triggered unhandled HTTP 500 crashes (['register_list', 'login_list', 'login_int_user', 'create_list', 'create_int_title', 'create_dict_desc', 'create_int_due', 'update_list']).

results.objective: Verify PUT /api/tasks/<id> rejects null/blank titles and malformed due_date cleanly with HTTP 400.
results.steps:
1. PUT /api/tasks/<id> with title=null.
2. PUT with whitespace-only title.
3. PUT with invalid due_date.
results.expected_result: All three invalid partial updates are rejected with HTTP 400.
results.actual_result: PUT title=null -> HTTP 500 (IntegrityError); PUT title='   ' -> HTTP 200 (accepted blank title); PUT bad due_date -> HTTP 500.

results.technique: Server-Side Web Form Validation & Persistent Crash Check
results.objective: Verify server-side Web UI form validation rejects whitespace titles and malformed due_date values.
results.steps:
1. Submit POST /tasks/new with blank title.
2. Submit POST /tasks/new with invalid due_date.
3. Request GET /.
results.expected_result: Server rejects invalid inputs with HTTP 400/validation error; GET / stays HTTP 200.
results.actual_result: Empty-title POST returned HTTP 302 (accepted); invalid due_date POST returned HTTP 302 and broke GET / with HTTP 500.

results.objective: Verify Web UI search query uses parameterized LIKE ? and resists SQLi unlike GET /api/tasks?q=.
results.preconditions: User A and User B exist with separate tasks.
results.steps:
1. Send same boolean SQLi payload used in TC-SEC-005 to Web UI GET /?q=.
2. Inspect HTTP status and HTML body.
results.expected_result: HTTP 200 rendered with no tasks from User B.
results.actual_result: Web UI returned HTTP 200; leaked_user_b=False (parameterized LIKE ? protected Web UI).

results.objective: Verify a captured session cookie is invalidated server-side after the user logs out.
results.preconditions: Session cookie captured prior to GET /logout in TC-SEC-009.
results.test_data: Captured pre-logout session cookie replayed against GET /api/dashboard
results.steps:
1. Capture session cookie before logout.
2. Execute GET /logout.
3. Replay captured cookie to GET /api/dashboard.
results.expected_result: Server rejects replayed pre-logout token with HTTP 401.
results.actual_result: Replayed pre-logout cookie still authenticated to GET /api/dashboard with HTTP 200 (stateless cookie lacks server-side revocation).

results.feature: Password Strength Policy & Request Size Limit (helpers.py, app.py)
results.objective: Verify password validator accepts 8-char spec minimum, rejects whitespace-only passwords, and bounds request/password size.
results.preconditions: Application running with default helpers.py and Flask config.
results.test_data: is_valid_password('Pass1234'), POST /api/register with 9-space password '         ', MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH check
results.steps:
1. Check 8-char spec minimum.
2. Register with 9 whitespace chars.
3. Check app.config['MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH'].
results.expected_result: 8-char passwords accepted; whitespace-only rejected; MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH configured.
results.actual_result: 8-char valid=False (corroborates Week 1 DEF-001 / Week 2 DEF-WB-001); whitespace-only 9-space password accepted=True (HTTP 201); MAX_CONTENT_LENGTH=None.
